rules.name: account-id
rules.human_description: A account-id value is a string with no further runtime constraints; the type exists to keep raw strings from being mistaken for one.

premises.rationale: X is typed string; the target language's type system rejects non-string values at construction.

rules.name: account-state
rules.human_description: A account-state bundles 2 fields (Id, Balance) into a single typed value.

premises.rationale: Id is typed account-id; values of that type can only be constructed via shengen's guarded constructor, which enforces all of account-id's premises transitively.
Balance is typed amount; values of that type can only be constructed via shengen's guarded constructor, which enforces all of amount's premises transitively.

rules.name: amount
rules.human_description: A amount value is a number that satisfies 1 additional constraint(s) checked at construction.

premises.rationale: X is typed number; the target language's type system rejects non-number values at construction.
shengen's generated constructor for amount rejects inputs that do not satisfy (>= X 0), so this premise holds for any value of type amount reachable in the impl.

rules.name: balance-invariant
rules.human_description: A balance-invariant is a multi-field structure whose constructor enforces 1 cross-field invariant(s).

premises.rationale: Bal is typed number; the target language's type system rejects non-number values at construction.
Tx is typed transaction; values of that type can only be constructed via shengen's guarded constructor, which enforces all of transaction's premises transitively.
shengen's generated constructor for balance-invariant rejects inputs that do not satisfy (>= Bal (head Tx)), so this premise holds for any value of type balance-invariant reachable in the impl.

rules.name: processable
rules.human_description: A pure function processable : amount --> (list transaction) --> boolean. The Shen spec is the oracle; the impl is asserted to match it on every sampled input.

premises.rationale: shen-derive evaluated the spec on 35 sampled cases (deterministic-default) and emitted a Go test asserting impl returns the same value on each.

rules.name: safe-transfer
rules.human_description: A safe-transfer bundles 2 fields (Tx, Check) into a single typed value.

premises.rationale: Tx is typed transaction; values of that type can only be constructed via shengen's guarded constructor, which enforces all of transaction's premises transitively.
Check is typed balance-checked; values of that type can only be constructed via shengen's guarded constructor, which enforces all of balance-checked's premises transitively.

rules.name: transaction
rules.human_description: A transaction bundles 3 fields (Amount, From, To) into a single typed value.

premises.rationale: Amount is typed amount; values of that type can only be constructed via shengen's guarded constructor, which enforces all of amount's premises transitively.
From is typed account-id; values of that type can only be constructed via shengen's guarded constructor, which enforces all of account-id's premises transitively.
To is typed account-id; values of that type can only be constructed via shengen's guarded constructor, which enforces all of account-id's premises transitively.
